transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to address the twenty-four drums of solvent waste from the recent line-cleaning operation currently secured in the hazardous-waste cage. As you all know, the temporary storage permit for these drums expires on Friday, so we need to move on disposition. Per our waste-closeout policy, before I can record a disposition decision, I need Jon to present the current laboratory and waste-log information for these drums, and Priya to present the current batch-genealogy and hold information. Plant policy favors solvent recovery if the material meets the approved recovery specification, and we'll need documented treatment for every drum removed from the cage. Let's get started with the review.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I received the laboratory classification report yesterday. 15 drums meet the approved solvent-recovery specification, 3 drums fail the water-content limit and must go to hazardous-waste incineration, and the remaining 6 drums were not classified in that report. A laboratory-system outage has kept the report from being uploaded to the waste log, so the waste log does not yet reflect these results.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My batch-genealogy review is complete. The 6 unclassified drums are from lot VX-204, and they contain residual catalyst. These drums must be retained on site for exactly 30 days for a possible process investigation rather than being sent for treatment. I should note that the hold tags have not yet been entered in the production system, but the genealogy review itself is complete.
transcript.speaker: A3
